title: The Long Letter
premise: In the winter of 1917, widowed lighthouse keeper Casper Okonkwo keeps a coastal town's unofficial ledger of debts, births, and promises — including a marriage vow he made to Amara, a lighthouse inspector's daughter now stranded on the wrong side when the army requisitions the coast and declares her family enemy aliens. When the requisitioning officer, Captain Voss, confiscates the ledger as evidence and begins using its names to settle old scores, Casper must choose between the law that protects his post and the promise that defines him. Smuggling Amara through the storm-battered coves while the armistice negotiations stall, he discovers the ledger was never just record-keeping — it was the town's conscience. The book ends with the armistice signed but justice unfinished: Casper burns the official copy of the ledger to protect the townsfolk, keeping only one page — the record of his own promise — which he finally delivers in person.
about_author: Odile Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal municipal records from the First World War era. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught between paperwork and conscience.

chapters.title: What the Light Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes his routines: tending the lamp, recording the town's informal ledger of names and promises, and his quiet grief for his late wife. A letter arrives from Amara, posted before war closed the routes, renewing a peacetime promise. Emotional beat: tenderness buried under duty.

chapters.title: The Requisition
chapters.summary: Captain Voss arrives with orders claiming the town, its boats, and all records 'for the duration.' Casper hands over the official registers but hides the personal ledger inside the lighthouse's oil store. POV alternates between Casper and Voss, who is more bureaucrat than brute. Beat: dread arriving politely.

chapters.title: Names Are Evidence
chapters.summary: Voss begins summoning townsfolk whose names appear in seized papers; an old fisherman is detained over a decades-old debt dispute. Casper realizes the ledger's hidden pages could either condemn or save people. His POV. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Enemy's Daughter
chapters.summary: A smuggler brings word that Amara is interned at a holding depot two coves north, awaiting deportation. Flashbacks reveal their promise made during the last peaceful summer. Casper's POV. Beat: love resurfacing as an obligation he cannot legally honor.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: The great storms begin; the army commandeers the lifeboat, leaving the coast unprotected. Casper rescues wrecked sailors against orders, earning the town's wary loyalty and Voss's suspicion. Casper's POV with a tense rescue sequence. Beat: defiance becoming habit.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Oil and Ink
chapters.summary: Voss confronts Casper, suspecting hidden documents, and offers a trade: the ledger's pages in exchange for travel permits. Casper stalls, copying names by lamplight. Alternating POV reveals Voss's own compromised position — he answers to superiors who demand results. Beat: cat-and-mouse with mutual respect.

chapters.title: The Long Letter
chapters.summary: Casper writes Amara a letter he cannot send, confessing everything — his wife's death, the promise, the plan forming. The chapter braids the unsent letter with his preparations: forged passes, tide charts, a boat hidden beneath the pier. Casper's POV. Beat: confession as courage.

chapters.title: Armistice, Almost
chapters.summary: Rumors of peace spread, then collapse as negotiations stall; Voss receives orders to deport the internees immediately. Casper learns Amara will be moved within days. Told partly through the town's voices as they decide, one by one, to help despite the risk. Beat: collective courage.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Climax. During the worst storm of the year, Casper extinguishes his own light to mislead the patrol boat and guides Amara and two others through black water to a waiting trawler. Voss discovers the deception mid-crossing and must choose whether to fire the signal flare. He doesn't. Beat: sacrifice answered by unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: One Page
chapters.summary: Resolution. The armistice is signed; Voss departs without filing charges, leaving Casper the confiscated ledger's official copy. Casper burns it to erase the debts and denunciations it contains, keeping only the page bearing his own promise. He travels inland to deliver it — and himself — to Amara. Beat: peace as something built, not declared.
